headline: The reported order<=5 flagship vacuum no-go is equivalent to a compact hypergraph/monomial-ideal statement: every d/bd singlet-support hyperedge contains at least one mu-support hyperedge. Equivalently I_d is contained in I_mu, so the mu-suppressed squarefree-VEV locus V(I_mu) lies inside the d-mass-vanishing locus V(I_d).

equivalent_forms.vacuum: for every active set T: if no mu support is contained in T, then no d/bd support is contained in T
equivalent_forms.hypergraph: for every d/bd support D_j there exists a mu support M_i with M_i subset D_j

proof.A_implies_B: take T=D_j; if D_j contained no mu support, T would be mu-free while D_j survives
proof.B_implies_A: a surviving D_j contains a surviving M_i, contradicting mu suppression
proof.B_iff_C: a squarefree monomial x^D belongs to the monomial ideal generated by x^M exactly when some M is a subset of D

physics_reading: At support level the d-type exotic mass operators are algebraically downstream of the mu-generating support ideal: any Boolean VEV choice that zeros the mu generators also zeros every tested d/bd generator. Higher-order operators can escape only by adding support monomials not divisible by the measured mu generators.

reproducibility_boundary.exact_part: the equivalence theorem and its deduction from the committed aggregate premise
reproducibility_boundary.next_required_artifact: raw orbifolder coupling support export; then the no-go reduces to 144 direct subset/divisibility checks instead of a 2^19 vacuum scan
